S1.hook: When does this patient go home?
S1.dek: A quality improvement study compared two ways of answering it at Houston Methodist, and reported which one was closer.

S2.dek: The hospital's own staff, and a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the EHR, over inpatient encounters discharged in the window below.

S3.dek: At admission the case managers and the tool sat within a fraction of a day of each other on error.
labels: MEAN ABSOLUTE ERROR IN DAYS, AT ADMISSION
bodies: The case managers did match the exact date more often, 23.6% against 15.3%.

S4.hook: On the last day, they were not
S4.dek: The authors say this is the point where an accurate date counts for most in bed management.
labels: WITHIN ONE DAY OF THE TRUE DATE 24 HOURS BEFORE DISCHARGE

S5.dek: Mean absolute error in days. The two never meet.
labels: HIGHER IS FURTHER FROM THE TRUE DATE
The study's authors, on their own result
bodies: The strong admission correlation did not persist nearer discharge and should not be interpreted as evidence that the tool captured the same information clinicians use throughout the stay.

S7.dek: Estimates were part of usual care and visible to care teams. They may be partly self-fulfilling. The authors' own word for it is advantaged nearer discharge.
labels: THE STUDY'S AUTHORS, AGAINST THEIR OWN RESULT
bodies: Accessible in the EHR but not enabled automatically.

labels: THE STUDY FOLLOWED THE SQUIRE REPORTING GUIDELINE
bodies: No baseline patient demographic data were available.

S9.dek: The authors say what has to happen before anyone decides the tool's extra accuracy in some subgroups justifies the complexity of putting it in.
